title: Introduce subscriber-driven sampling proxy to minimize tracing hot-path allocations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: after the runtime 1.18 tracer bump we observed a ~8% p99 latency regression in inference-ingress under high QPS. Root cause: synchronous span encoding and reservoir sampling decisions in the request hot path allocate transient buffers and take mutexes. Proposal: implement a lightweight subscriber-driven sampling proxy (SDSP) — a compact, lock-free hot-path shim that emits small 'sampling hint' tokens into a bounded ring and defers heavier decisions (encoding, reservoir commit) to a background controller. The SDSP will be language-agnostic (gRPC + protobuf) and shippable as a minimal runtime sidecar or library. Goals: eliminate allocations on warm path, reduce per-request CPU by 15-25%, maintain tail-sampling accuracy, provide per-tenant budgeting.
acceptance_criteria: Hot-path allocations attributable to tracer reduce by >= 70% in microbenchmark
P99 end-to-end latency for inference-ingress returns to baseline (+/-1%) under synthetic high QPS
Sampling decisions for tail events match existing reservoir algorithm within 5% variance
Canary rollout run for 48 hours with no increase in error rate or SLO violations
Documentation and API spec published in Confluence and SDKs updated
tasks: Design proto for sampling-hint token and bounded ring buffer
Implement SDSP C++/Go sidecar with lock-free ring and fast-path no-op when sampling disabled
Background controller service to consume ring, apply reservoir/tail-sampling, and emit commit events
Integrate with existing trace-collector and add per-tenant budget metering
Add metrics: sdsp.hotpath.allocations, sdsp.ring.depth, sdsp.drop_count, sampling.controller.latency
Add e2e canary pipeline and dashboard panels for rollout
Write library wrappers for node/python/go shells to adopt SDSP
